jobs.description:
TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.
Within the DFG-funded interdisciplinary research unit GArua: “Fog-dependent water relations and plant invasion in the Galápagos Archipelago under climate change” (https://www.uni-marburg.de/en/prfolder-en/news/when-the-garua-disappears-a-new-research-unit-will-study-the-future-of-the-galapagos-cloud-forests), the Faculty of Environmental Sciences, Department of Forest Sciences, Institute of Forest Botany and Forest Zoology, Chair of Forest Botany offers a position as

Research Associate / PhD Student (m/f/x)
in Tropical tree ecophysiology and tree water relations
(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited until July 31, 2030, with the possibility of extension up to a total employment duration of four years and entails 65% of the full-time weekly hours. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification (usually PhD). Within this collaborative research project, the research associate will be responsible for the installation and maintenance of sap flow sensors and automated dendrometers for quantifying tree water use and status of native and exotic shrub and tree species, for hydraulic characterization as well as for several measurement campaigns.
an excellent university degree in forest or plant ecology, ecophysiology, environmental sciences, or a related discipline with field and/or lab experience
willingness for several long-term stays at the Charles Darwin Research Station, main island of the Galapagos Archipelago, Ecuador, as well as to familiarize oneself with technical installations and sensor networks
capability for intensive fieldwork campaigns in harsh environmental conditions is essential while advanced understanding of tree water relations is a plus
proven scientific writing skills is essential, while advanced knowledge in statistical analyses with R is a plus
proven experience in working in diverse teams, team-oriented and willing to learn and work independently
advanced command of English is essential while basic knowledge of Spanish and/or German is desirable

joint doctoral studies together with further PhD student in other subprojects working on Galapagos
an inspiring, international and interdisciplinary working environment, specialized in forest and plant ecology, ecophysiology and plant hydraulics
attractive working conditions and opportunities for further professional development at TUD

For project-related questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Bernhard Schuldt (bernhard.schuldt@tu-dresden.de).

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of decentralized security

Join a World-Class Research Team in Information Security The Chair for Information Security at Ruhr University Bochum — led by Prof. Dr. Ghassan Karame and part of the Faculty of Computer Science since 2021 — brings together an international, multicultural team of researchers pushing the boundaries of decentralized and systems security. Our work spans a broad spectrum of security and privacy challenges, with a particular emphasis on decentralized security and distributed machine learning security. We are proud to be affiliated with: • Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI), one of Europe's most respected centers for fundamental research in computer security. Founded over two decades ago, HGI maintains deep collaborations with world-renowned academic institutions, industry leaders, and media partners — and has been a launchpad for numerous successful cybersecurity startups. CASA — Cluster of Excellence: Securing the Digital Society is a leading center for cybersecurity research at Ruhr University Bochum. Through an innovative and interdisciplinary research program, CASA strengthens the resilience of the digital society, bringing together internationally renowned researchers to develop next-generation security solutions that holistically protect large-scale socio-technical systems, spanning cryptography, hardware and software, and the intersection of technology with users and society. Funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) with €53 million for its second phase from 2026 to 2032, CASA is hosted at the Horst Görtz Institute (HGI) at RUB and partnered with the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy (MPI-SP).

The Chair for Information Security has an immediate full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of (decentralized) systems security (currently 39.83 hours /week = 100%).

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 Jahre
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-11-02

Your tasks:

- The main task in this position is to research, analyze, and improve the security and privacy of modern decentralized platforms while enhancing their performance and scalability.
- Members of Prof. Karame's Chair conduct research and teaching in various areas of IT security. The Chair offers various courses in the Bachelor's and Master’s degree programs and participates in several third-party-funded projects.
- This international and dynamic team also cooperates with several university and non-university institutions (e.g., the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy).

Your profile:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related field
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills in English
- Background in the areas of IT security and privacy, system security, and distributed systems is a plus.
- Experience in software development including experience with programming languages, such as Python, Golang, Java, or C/C++ is also a plus.

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1

Doctoral Position (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience (Project Z02)

Are you curious about how the human brain stores and retrieves memories? You want bridge the gap between academia and the wider public? The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information.

We are actively seeking a talented PhD student to join our science communication project within the CRC 1844, which develops a digital serious game for citizen science, establishing a bidirectional bridge between episodic memory (EM) research and the general public. On the one hand, the game facilitates dissemination and intervention studies, with the public being involved in game design and extensions. On the other hand, the game allows for large-scale EM data collection from a diverse population. It also enables longitudinal research on EM, as well as prospective studies of EM changes preceding psychopathology.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)
Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval
Apply by:  2026-11-02

Your tasks:

- The primary task will be the analysis of the behavioral data from gamified EM tasks, development of novel analyses, and interpretation of the results
- Help adapt laboratory experiments into a serious game setting in collaboration with the Cologne Game Lab
- Help validate the collected EM data in collaboration with experimental projects in the CRC 1844
- Assist the outreach coordinator associated with this project with player recruitment and outreach activities
- Correlate memory performance data from the game with demographic and psychological data in collaboration with the DZPG (German Center for Mental Health)
- Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations with experimental and computational neuroscientists, psychologists, and philosophers
- Present your results and findings in international conferences and scientific journals

Your profile:

- An excellent master’s degree, or equivalent, in computational neuroscience, physics, mathematics, computer science, or a related field
- Ability to work independently
- Competence in mathematical modeling and statistical analysis
- Excellent programming skills, e.g., Python
- Relevant research experience in neuroscience or a related field
- Excellent communication skills in English
- Team spirit
- Experience working within a collaborative research group (optional)

The Department of Pediatric Oncology, Hematology and Clinical Immunology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU), headed by Prof. Dr. Arndt Borkhardt, is one of the leading clinical centers for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer in Germany. The clinic is part of the University Tumor Center (UTZ) at the UKD and the Center for Integrative Oncology Aachen-Bonn-Cologne-Düsseldorf (CIO-ABCD), which is funded by the German Cancer Aid. It is a founding partner of the German Consortium for Translational Cancer Research (DKTK) Essen-Düsseldorf and participates in international research consortia and study groups. The clinic operates a fully equipped research laboratory (safety level 1 and 2 according to the Genetic Engineering/Biotechnology Ordinance, including a GMP, next generation sequencing, flow cytometry, life cell imaging, and high-throughput drug testing facility) with 5 research groups and >30 staff working in an interdisciplinary manner on the fundamentals of childhood cancer and in the field of therapy optimization. We are seeking a highly motivated and creative PhD Student to join our research program in the field of amino acid homeostasis and cancer metabolism, with an anticipated start date of 02/2027. The successful candidate will work on the ERC-funded project “POWERFUL” (Deciphering how cancer cells fuel themselves to advance personalized treatment strategies).
The PhD student will take a leading role in understanding how cancer cells sense and respond to amino acid availability, and how to translate this knowledge into precision-based treatment strategies. This position requires scientific independence and the opportunity to contribute intellectually to experimental design, data interpretation, and publication strategy. The candidate will employ and further develop advanced experimental models and methodologies, including organoid systems, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, multiparameter flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, FRET assays, protein interaction and signaling assays, as well as in vitro and in vivo drug screening approaches.
Candidates should have a very good understanding of and experience with standard molecular biology techniques including but not limited to tissue culture, genome editing, FACS analysis, confocal microscopy, immunoblot, and PCR/qPCR. Experience with animal models is a plus (as is FELASA B certification). Willingness to learn and work with murine experimental models is a fundamental requirement. - Master in natural sciences or related field

- Solid experience with cancer models (e.g. organoids, PDXs) and drug-response studies
- expertise in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including mammalian tissue culture, genome editing, FACS/flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and PCR/qPCR.

- Excellent written and spoken English language skills, German language skills are a plus

- Willingness to cooperate and ability to work in a team
- Experience in working with animals (FELASA B) is a plus, willingness to work with animals a requisite Remuneration is based on TV-L in pay grade 13 (65%), taking into account all previous periods of employment. The employment contract will be concluded with Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ) is the Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. The DDZ is an interdisciplinary research center linking molecular and cell biological basic with clinical and epidemiological research approaches. The DDZ has the aim to develop new approaches for prevention, early detection and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and to improve therapy and treatment of its complications.
The Institute for Clinical Diabetology (Director: Prof. Dr. Michael Roden) is looking for an

Epidemiologist (postdoc - m/f/d) We are searching for a candidate with (1) a doctoral degree in epidemiology, (bio)statistics or a comparable discipline, (2) the ability to work in an interdisciplinary manner with physicians and life scientists, and (3) knowledge of epidemiological methodology and statistical analysis systems (e.g. SAS or R). In addition, excellent writing and communication skills in English are required. Experience in the analysis of proteomics data would be desirable.

The project will be a collaboration between the research group Inflammation (Prof. Dr. Christian Herder) and the Clinical Study Center (Prof. Dr. Robert Wagner, PD Dr. Oana-Patricia Zaharia) at DDZ. Tasks include planning epidemiological analyses within different cohort studies, performing statistical analyses in projects related to the link between inflammation, diabetes and cardiovascular complications, and communicating results in conferences and publications. The coordination of projects with internal and external partners is important as the position will be linked to projects with the Department of Cardiology, Pulmonology and Vascular Medicine at the Medical Faculty, Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.
An exciting and diversified fulltime job in a multidisciplinary team. The project should start on the earliest possible start date with a 3-year-contract.
A salary as based on qualification and experience according to TV-L in its current version for North Rhine-Westphalia.
Family-friendly working conditions and equal gender policy. Since May 2011, the DDZ is a “Career and Family” audit-acknowledged center.

jobs.occupation: RESEARCH ASSOCIATE / DOCTORAL STUDENT (f/m/d) for the research Project "multidimensional analytic... (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
As a university of applied sciences, we are particularly committed to
sustainable development. Based on our sustainability strategy, we integrate
sustainability into all degree programs, applied research, and our daily
operations. With our campuses in Bochum and Heiligenhaus, we provide important
impulses for the regional development of society and the economy. Numerous
collaborations underline our international focus. We aim to enhance the quality
of our teaching and research by appointing further dedicated and innovative
researchers.

In the Physiotherapy Division of the Department of Nursing, Midwifery and
Therapy Sciences at Hochschule Bochum (Bochum University of Applied Sciences),
a four-year position is available at the earliest possible date, and no later
than March 2027, as

RESEARCH ASSOCIATE / DOCTORAL STUDENT (f/m/d) for the research Project
"multidimensional analytical approaches to improve LBP diagnosis and prognosis"
as part of the DFG Research Unit "DYN3M" (EG 13 TV-L)

The Project is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The position
is fixed-term for a period of 4 years for academic qualification, with a focus
on multimodal data analysis in low back pain. Remuneration is paid in grade E13
TV-L, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The working hours
comprise 23 hours and 54 minutes per week (60% of a full-time position). As
part of this project, a cooperative doctorate at the Doctoral School NRW (PK
NRW) is envisaged.

The DFG-funded research project "DYN3M" (2026–2030) investigates the dynamic
mechanisms of musculoskeletal health and the chronification of low back pain in
order to drive the transition from generic treatment approaches to precise,
personalized pain therapy. As part of your doctorate, you will work at the
intersection of neuroscience, biomechanics, and data science to examine the
interplay between the musculoskeletal system, neural movement control, and
psychological factors. In doing so, you will apply machine learning and
artificial intelligence methods to analyze multimodal data, identify
high-dimensional signatures, and develop predictive models to evaluate whether
individual healing trajectories exist and examing whether specific subgroups
exist for targeted treatments to optimize overall therapeutic success.

Responsibilities:

- Project coordination and operational implementation of the project.
- In addition to project coordination with national and international
partners, the project includes conducting subprojects as part of your doctorate.
- Learning and implementing quantitative data collection and analysis
methods, including machine learning, as well as coordinating and drafting
peer-reviewed publications.
- Participating in the development and application of state-of-the-art data
science models in close collaboration with consortium partners from
biomechanics, medicine, and psychology/psychosomatics.
- Presenting research findings at national and international conferences and
symposia.
- Implementing modern data management standards and, where possible, open
science publication of research outputs (metadata, analytical workflows, code,
documentation, etc.) in compliance with the FAIR principles (Findable,
Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).

You lead the commodity agenda for a commodity for Large Steam and Syncon products. * Deliver measurable value (CNI/savings, total cost improvements, inventory and cash objectives) and maintain transparent KPIs and spend dashboards for your area

* Proven ability to lead cross functional commodity teams (Commodity Circle) and influence at multiple levels, internally and at suppliers
* Proficiency with ERP/MRP and eSourcing platforms; comfort with KPI dashboards and data driven decisions. (Experience within Siemens Energy procurement frameworks is a plus.)

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Postdoc (m/f/d) in Endosymbiosis Research
Job-ID: J000000668
Working hours: Full time
Location: Düsseldorf
Start date: 01.01.2027
Limited until: 31.12.2028
Apply till: 21.10.2026
Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L
Organization: MathematischNaturwissenschaftliche Fakultät
Job Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Our work has provided exciting insights into organellogenesis and enabled us to develop novel tools for dissecting the molecular and cellular biology of host-symbiont interactions (see e.g., Morales et al. (2023) Curr Biol. doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.020.; Sørensen et al. (2024) FEBS J. doi: 10.1111/febs.17356; Maurya et al. (2025) Science Adv. doi: 10.1126/sciadv.adp8518; Klimenko et al. (2025) Plant Phys. doi: 10.1093/plphys/kiaf504; Hammond et al. (2026) Nat Commun. doi: 10.1038/s41467-026-70084-0.). The successful candidate will contribute to a current project at the heart of our research program, with the opportunity to shape the project in part according to their scientific interests, expertise, and strengths. The position will also involve a limited amount of undergraduate teaching in German [4 contact hours (Semesterwochenstunden) per week], providing an opportunity to contribute to the training of the next generation of biologists.
A PhD in biology, biochemistry or a related area
An excellent academic track record
Research experience in microbiology or cell biology, genetic engineering, and advanced microscopy techniques
Experience with organelle biology, symbioses or protistology is a plus
A strong motivation in experimental work, literature search and scientific writing
Readiness to work independently and as a team player in an interdisciplinary, international team
Fluency (oral and written) in English and German
Proactive character, creativity, communication and presentation skills, excellent organization and analytical skills
The position is initially limited for a period of 2 years with the possibility of extension. It is a qualification position in the sense of the Act of Academic Fixed-Term Contract (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG), which is to promote the scientific qualification of the employee. The pay scale grouping will be 13 TV-L.
